A Weekend on the Coast Trail

Two days, 28 kilometres, three beaches and one very windy headland. Everything you need to plan an easy coastal hike.

By the Trailhead editors · 9 min read

The Coast Trail is the kind of walk that makes a weekend feel twice as long. It follows the cliffs for most of its length, drops to the sand three times, and finishes at a small harbour town with good coffee and a bus back to the start. You don't need much experience, but you do need to plan around the tides.

This guide covers the route in two days, with a night at the halfway campground. If you'd rather stay indoors, there are a handful of guesthouses in the village at kilometre 15.

The route at a glance

SectionDistanceClimbTime
North beach to Lookout Point6.5 km240 m2 h
Lookout Point to Cove Camp8.0 km310 m2 h 45
Cove Camp to the Headland7.5 km420 m3 h
The Headland to Harbour Town6.0 km150 m1 h 45
Check the tide tableThe beach crossing after Lookout Point is only passable within two hours of low tide. Plan your start time around it, not the other way round.

Day one: beaches and the lookout

Start early from the north beach car park. The first hour is flat and sandy, then the path climbs steadily through coastal heath to Lookout Point, where the whole route unfolds to the south. On a clear day you can see the headland you'll be crossing tomorrow.

After the lookout, the trail drops back to the shore for the tidal crossing. Rock pools here are full of anemones and small crabs, so leave time to wander. The final stretch to Cove Camp is shaded and gentle, a welcome end to the day.

Where to sleep

Cove Camp has twelve tent sites, a water tap and a composting toilet. Sites can't be booked, so arrive by mid-afternoon in summer. The beach below the camp is sheltered and good for a sunset swim.

The best part of the trail is the hour before sunset at Cove Camp, when the wind drops and the whole bay turns gold.

Day two: over the headland

The second day is shorter but steeper. The climb to the headland starts right out of camp and gains most of its height in the first three kilometres. Take it slowly: the views back along the coast are the best of the trip, and there are benches at the two main switchbacks.

From the top, the path follows the ridge before descending through farmland to Harbour Town. The last kilometre runs along the sea wall, past the fishing boats and straight to the bakery.

What to pack

  • Sturdy shoes with good grip for the wet rocks on the tidal crossing
  • A wind layer, even in summer; the headland is always breezy
  • Two litres of water per person, refilled at Cove Camp
  • Sun protection and a hat, since most of the trail has no shade
  • A printed copy of the tide table and the route map

Getting there and back

A weekend bus runs from Harbour Town to the north beach twice each morning, which means you can park at the finish and ride to the start. Outside the summer season, the bus only runs on Saturdays, so check the timetable before you go.

If you're driving, the north beach car park fills quickly on sunny weekends. Arrive before nine, or use the overflow field a few hundred metres up the road.

Good to know

Dogs are welcome on a lead, except on the beaches between May and September when shorebirds are nesting. Fires aren't allowed anywhere on the trail. Mobile reception is patchy between Lookout Point and the headland, so tell someone your plans before you set off.

Above all, take your time. The trail isn't long, and the slow moments, like a rock pool, a bench at the top of a climb or a swim at the end of the day, are what make it worth walking.
